In addition to equipment sales, the company fabricates custom cutting boards to customer-specified dimensions, offering a made-to-order service for foodservice operators.

The company serves restaurants, commercial kitchens, and broader foodservice operations, providing both standard equipment and tailored cutting board solutions. Its customer base includes independent eateries and institutional foodservice buyers seeking reliable supply.

RECO emphasizes affordable pricing, durability, and reliability across its product lines, backed by partnerships with established manufacturers. The family-owned structure underscores a commitment to quality standards and customer satisfaction in every transaction.

name: Restronics Southeast
old_description: We are a consultative OEM sales rep organization, where we help educate our customers to improve their processes and productivity.
about:
Restronics Southeast operates from Acworth, Georgia, and was founded in 1991. The firm is led by Managing Partner Tim Glasgow, who brings 35 years of industry experience.

The company functions as a national manufacturers' representative for the electronic manufacturing sector, representing suppliers across a territory that includes Georgia, Alabama, Tennessee, Mississippi, and Arkansas. Its consultative sales engineers provide no‑charge ESD facility assessments, workstation evaluations, static bag testing, and assembly line consultations covering both surface‑mount (SMT) and through‑hole processes.

Customers are primarily OEMs and contract manufacturers seeking to improve productivity, reduce field failures, and optimize capital investment in assembly operations. The team helps identify ESD‑vulnerable components, recommends process efficiencies, and manages distribution channel relationships for the principals it represents.

Restronics was started to give manufacturers honest, timely information that increases profitability, emphasizing credibility with both customers and the factories it represents.

old_description: Our Auburn, Indiana-based company was founded in 1976 and continues to grow steadily. Our company has provided medical instrumentation to the orthopaedic industry for more than 45 years.
about:
Revelation Medical Devices was founded in 1976 in Auburn, Indiana, and has operated continuously from that location for nearly five decades. The company began as a supplier of medical instrumentation to the orthopaedic industry and has expanded its capabilities over time.

Today the firm provides end-to-end medical device contract manufacturing, covering design, development, prototyping, and production. Its shop runs 3-, 4-, and 5-axis milling, live-tool turning, orthopaedic-quality finishing, a dedicated plastics manufacturing cell, laser and TIG welding, laser etching, passivation, polishing, and non-sterile packaging and labeling. The facility serves projects from prototype through full-scale production, though specific headcount and floor space are not disclosed.

Customers include large and small orthopaedic OEMs as well as medical-device startups. The company emphasizes its proximity to Warsaw, Indiana — known as the orthopaedic capital — which allows close collaboration with clients in that cluster.

Revelation Medical Devices states that its mission is to empower medical device innovators through ISO-certified, high-precision manufacturing delivered with reliability, flexibility, and excellence. Core values cited are excellence, integrity, teamwork, and compassion, and the company highlights its FDA registration and ISO 13485:2016 certification as foundations of its quality system.

name: Revolution Bag
old_description: Delta Plastics of the South is founded in Stuttgart, Arkansas, with a focus on providing efficient irrigation solutions to farmers in the Mid-South, and soon after starts recycling to show the importance of being part of the solution to plastic waste.
about:
Revolution Bag, operating as Revolution Company, traces its roots to 1996 when Delta Plastics of the South was founded in Stuttgart, Arkansas. The company began by supplying efficient irrigation solutions to farmers in the Mid-South region and quickly added recycling operations to address plastic waste. In 2008 the business expanded to Little Rock, where it established its first sustainable-loop recycling facility and launched the Revolution Bag line of trash can liners made with up to 97% certified post-consumer resin. The headquarters remain in Little Rock, Arkansas.

Today Revolution manufactures a range of plastic products including trash can liners, carryout bags for foodservice and retail, agricultural films, commercial sheeting, and stretch films. The company runs an integrated circular model: a specialized fleet collects used film, which is cleaned and mechanically recycled at its facilities to produce certified post-consumer and post-industrial resins. Those resins feed both Revolution’s own product lines and the supply chains of global brands and OEMs. The company reports processing more than 300 million pounds of material annually and has diverted over 3 billion pounds from landfills since inception. Growth has come through acquisitions such as Rodeo Plastic Bag & Film, Command Packaging, Encore Recycling, Pak-Sher, Polar Plastics, Jadcore, and Five Point Films, adding capacity in commercial films, consumer bags, post-industrial recycling, and stretch films.

Revolution serves agriculture, food service, construction and commercial supply, consumer goods, restaurants, delis, and grocery chains. Its recycled resins are sold to brands and original equipment manufacturers seeking circular content. A noted reference comes from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, where a sustainability manager reported reducing virgin resin use from hundreds of thousands of pounds to 17,000 pounds annually through Revolution’s programs.

The company was started to demonstrate that plastic can be a valuable resource with infinite usefulness if reclaimed responsibly. Its stated differentiator is a closed-loop business model that controls the entire lifecycle — from collection and recycling to resin production and finished goods — enabling customers to meet ESG goals while maintaining product performance.

The business designs and builds custom furniture and accents — such as reclaimed barn‑wood mantels — using salvaged lumber and other reclaimed stock. Services include a design studio where clients collaborate with reclamation experts, direct sales of salvaged wood for DIY projects, and a mobile on‑site design and installation consultation service for residential and commercial spaces.

Reworx serves homeowners, interior designers, and commercial clients seeking sustainable, story‑rich pieces for both private residences and public spaces. The salvage and wood sales channel also caters to DIY enthusiasts looking for reclaimed material for their own projects.

The founders frame the venture around sustainability, craftsmanship, and environmental responsibility, aiming to combine timeless style with modern function so that each piece transforms a space while telling a meaningful story.

name: Rhino Wire Works, LLC
old_description: At Rhino Wire Works, clients can request custom wire forms, bringing their ideas to life in collaboration with our skilled engineers. We meticulously craft each wire form to meet specific requirements, turning imagination into tangible, high-quality results for industrial, commercial, and artistic purposes.
about:
Rhino Wire Works operates from Delavan, Wisconsin, where it was established in January 1994 as JB Wire Service, Inc. by John Burgstede. Burgstede brought over 40 years of experience from his uncle’s wire forming and stamping business, and together with George Jeninga they accumulated more than 70 years in the trade. In 2024 the company was acquired by Jonathan Zepeda, who contributes 20-plus years in the steel and metals industry and continues to collaborate with Burgstede.

The shop specializes in custom wire forming and bending, working from prints, sketches, or samples to take parts from prototype through full production runs. It produces OEM and service parts, designs and builds custom paint‑line fixtures and hooks (sold under the Rhino Hooks brand), and coordinates secondary operations through a network of partner machine shops.

Customers span industrial, commercial, and artistic sectors, ranging from large OEMs to small businesses needing wire forms, hanging fixtures, or specialty hooks for paint lines and material handling.

The company emphasizes fast quotes, quick delivery, competitive pricing, superior quality, and dependable service — a philosophy carried forward from its founding team and reinforced under the new ownership.

name: Rice Machinery Machine Tools SALES, Service
old_description: Rice Machinery specializes in selling new machine tools, CNC controls, custom building, refurbishing and modernizing used machinery for all manufacturing industries including schools and colleges. We stand by our products 100%, and are well known to take great pride in our work and customer satisfaction.
about:
Rice Machinery is based in Cranston, Rhode Island. The company traces its roots to 1968 when S. Arnold Rice established the business, originally known as Reynolds of Baker Street. Current owner Cory McLaughlin continues the operation, serving customers throughout New England.

The company operates as an authorized distributor for Sharp CNC machine tools and Acu-Rite G2 CNC controls, while also selling new and used repair parts, buying and trading used machinery, and providing retrofitting services that add 2- or 3-axis CNC technology to existing knee or bed mills. Its facilities include a 4,000-square-foot showroom, a 15,000-square-foot main warehouse, and three additional warehouses across Rhode Island, supported by an in-house CNC demonstration, parts, and rebuilding department with three service trucks making daily calls.

Rice Machinery serves a broad range of manufacturing industries as well as educational institutions such as schools and colleges across the New England region. Customers include job shops, production facilities, and academic programs seeking new or refurbished machine tools, CNC upgrades, and on-site repair or training.

The firm emphasizes its long-standing reputation for quality products and service that exceeds expectations, built on a tradition started in 1968 and maintained through hands-on technical support, including in-house and on-site CNC control training.

Customers include individual vehicle owners, repair shops, and restoration specialists seeking import and domestic parts across the United States. The company emphasizes service to the Kansas City metro area while fulfilling orders nationally through its eBay store and direct shipping.

Rich Industries highlights a 90-day warranty on all parts, extended warranty options, and a commitment to customer service that aims to simplify parts procurement. The firm positions itself as more than a parts counter by offering restoration, salvage sales, and locating services under one roof.

name: Richey Capacitor Inc.
old_description: R. Royce Richey entered in the electronics industry in 1954 and was influential in the design and development of the subminiature electrolytic capacitor for the US market. He founded the company in 1965, and Richey is still one of the most recognizable names in the electronic industry.
about:
Richey Capacitor Inc. is headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee. The company was founded in 1965 by R. Royce Richey, who had entered the electronics industry in 1954 and played a key role in developing the subminiature electrolytic capacitor for the U.S. market.

The company manufactures and markets aluminum electrolytic and film capacitors. Its product line includes computer-grade, snap-in, and through-hole aluminum electrolytic capacitors, as well as dipped and box-type film capacitors. Richey leverages manufacturing facilities in China and Taiwan, and provides custom part-number data sheets, samples, and extensive technical support to design engineers, purchasing agents, and distributors.

Richey serves the broader electronics industry and has built long-term relationships with companies such as Franklin Electric, Paul C Buff, QSC Audio, Aclara, Astronics Electronic Solutions, United Technologies, and Robertshaw Controls. Its customers span audio equipment, aerospace, industrial controls, and smart infrastructure sectors.

Richey emphasizes its thorough technical knowledge of capacitor technology, combined with advanced manufacturing capabilities from its overseas facilities. The company cites constant development of new materials and processes, along with a personal level of customer service and complete product information, as factors that have made it a successful American supplier for over 50 years.
